source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} and spoke{H559} to them again{H5750} in words{H1697} of parable{H4912}:

textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading stands here. Howard's note (22:1): 'At this point the Brit. Lib. ms again becomes our basic text; ms C also resumes at this point. Both number this פרק צ״א since the entirety of the last pereq was omitted. All other mss number this פרק צ״ב' — the base ms's section count betrays exactly where its lost leaf (21:33-46) fell.

verses.translation: The kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} is like{H1819} a king{H4428} who made{H6213} a chuppah{H2646}.

one_way_hebrew: חופה (H2646) — the bridal canopy: 'as a bridegroom coming out of his chuppah' (Ps 19:6); 'let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber, and the bride out of her chuppah' (Joel 2:16). The word recurs seven times through the parable (vv. 2,3,4,8,9,10,11,12) — the feast is a Hebrew wedding under the canopy; Greek γάμοι is generic festivity.
greek_deviations: No 'for his son': Greek Matthew reads 'a king who made a marriage FOR HIS SON'; the Shem Tov text has simply 'a king who made a chuppah.' The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew keeps 'a wedding for his son' with the Greek.

verses.translation: And he sent{H7971} his servants{H5650} for the called ones{H7121} to the chuppah{H2646}, but they were not willing{H14} toward him.

one_way_hebrew: ולא אבו (H14) — Scripture's refusal-verb for covenant unwillingness: 'ye would not (ולא אביתם) go up' (Deut 1:26); 'in returning and rest shall ye be saved... and ye would not (ולא אביתם)' (Isa 30:15). The called ones refuse in the Tanakh's own word for Israel's refusals.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:3): לו] לבא ABDEFG ('to come'), omit C.

verses.translation: And he sent{H7971} again{H5750} other{H312} servants{H5650}, saying{H559}: Say{H559} to the called ones{H7121}: Behold{H2009}, I have prepared{H3559} the feast{H4960} and slaughtered{H2076} oxen{H7794} and fowl{H5775}, and everything{H3605} is ready{H3559}; come{H935} to the chuppah{H2646}.

one_way_hebrew: משתה (H4960) — the royal banquet word of Esther (Esth 1:3; 2:18); וזבחתי (H2076) — the slaughter-verb that is also the sacrifice-verb: the king's feast is told in the vocabulary of the altar.
greek_deviations: 'Oxen and FOWL' (שורים ועופות) — Greek Matthew has 'my oxen and my fatlings (σιτιστά).'
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads אדרים; Howard's text reads אחרים, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (22:4): הכנתי] הכינותי ABDEFG; שורים ועופות] שור ועוף ABDEFG.

verses.translation: But they despised{H959} it and went off{H1980}, some{H7117} into the city{H5892} and some to their business.

one_way_hebrew: בזו (H959) — Esau's verb: 'thus Esau despised (ויבז) his birthright' (Gen 25:34). One word indicts the called ones with the firstborn who traded his inheritance for a meal.
מקצתם (H7117) — 'some of them': late-biblical Hebrew (Dan 1:2; Neh 7:70); עסק ('business') is rabbinic Hebrew outright — the author's living register.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:5): והם בזו] omit C, והם לא באו G ('they did not come'); בזו] בא D.

verses.translation: And the others{H312} took{H3947} his servants{H5650} and abused{H5953} them and killed them{H2026}.

one_way_hebrew: והתעללו (H5953) — the hithpael 'abuse, deal wantonly with' of Judg 19:25 and 1 Sam 31:4; Greek ὕβρισαν translates the idea, the Hebrew uses Scripture's own outrage-verb.
textual_notes: Howard prints לקחו את עבדיו in parentheses: the words are missing in the base ms and C, supplied from ABDEF (so his apparatus and the transcriber's footnote).

verses.translation: And the king{H4428} heard{H8085}, and his anger{H639} burned{H2734}, and he sent away{H7971} those{H1992} murderers{H7523}, and their house{H1004} he burned{H8313} with fire{H784}.

one_way_hebrew: ויחר אפו — 'his anger burned': the Torah's stock idiom (Gen 39:19; Exod 4:14); שרף באש — 'burned with fire,' the Torah's judgment formula (Deut 13:17, the condemned city; Josh 7:25).
greek_deviations: 'Their HOUSE he burned with fire' — Greek Matthew reads 'burned their CITY (πόλιν).' The base Hebrew also lacks the armies: mss ABDEFG add חיל וישמיד ('[sent] an army and destroyed'), assimilating to Greek's 'sent his armies and destroyed those murderers'; the base text has only 'he sent away those murderers.'
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads יושמע; Howard's text reads וישמע, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (22:7): וישלח] + חיל וישמיד ABDEFG; הרוצחים] ההורגים A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} he said{H559} to his servants{H5650}: The chuppah{H2646} is ready{H3559}, but{H7535} the called ones{H7121} were not worthy.

translation_notes: ראויים ('worthy, fitting') — again the post-biblical Hebrew adjective (cf. 20:4), the author's natural register.

verses.translation: And now{H6258} go out{H3318} to the roads{H1870}, and all{H3605} whom you find{H4672}, call{H7121} to the chuppah{H2646}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:9): ועתה] + לכו G.

verses.translation: And his servants{H5650} went out{H3318} to the roads{H1870} and gathered{H6908} all{H3605} who were found{H4672}, good{H2896} and bad{H7451}, and the chuppah{H2646} was filled{H4390} with those who ate{H398}.

one_way_hebrew: ויקבצו (H6908) — the prophets' ingathering verb (Isa 56:8, 'YHWH... who gathers the outcasts of Israel'; Ezek 36:24): the servants do to the road-people what God promises to do to the exiles.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:10): אל הדרכים] omit EF; הדרכים] + וימצאו G.

verses.translation: And the king{H4428} entered{H935} to see{H7200} the eaters{H398}, and saw{H7200} there{H8033} a man{H120} who was not clothed{H3847} in the garments{H899} of the chuppah{H2646}.

one_way_hebrew: בגדי החופה — wedding garments: the clothing symbol in its Hebrew home (Isa 61:10, 'he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation... as a bridegroom'); the unclothed guest stands against Isaiah's clothed bridegroom.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads האוכים; Howard's text reads האוכלים, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (22:11): מלובש] מלבוש D; G rewords with ראוי לחופה ('fit for the chuppah').

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to him: My beloved{H157}, how{H349} did you come{H935} in here without{H3808} the garments{H3830} of the chuppah{H2646}? And he kept silent{H2790}.

one_way_hebrew: אהובי — 'my beloved' again (as in 20:13) for Greek ἑταῖρε ('comrade'): the king's rebuke still speaks covenant affection.
החריש (H2790) — the loaded biblical silence (Gen 24:21; 34:5): he 'held his peace,' having no answer.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:12): אהובי] אדוני A ('my lord'); לכאן] בכאן A; החופה] חופה A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the king{H4428} said{H559} to his ministers{H8334}: Bind{H631} his hands{H3027} and his feet{H7272} and cast{H7993} him into lowest{H8482} Sheol{H7585}; and there{H8033} will be weeping{H1065} and gnashing{H2786} of teeth{H8127}.

one_way_hebrew: בשאול תחתית — 'into LOWEST SHEOL': the Torah's own phrase, 'a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest Sheol (שאול תחתית)' (Deut 32:22; cf. Ps 86:13, משאול תחתיה). The Hebrew names the destination from Moses' song.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew reads 'cast him into the OUTER DARKNESS (σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον)'; the Hebrew base text reads 'into lowest Sheol' (Deut 32:22). Mss ABDEFG read במחשכי תחתיות ('into the dark places of the depths' — Ps 88:7's language), moving toward the Greek picture; both readings are built from Tanakh phrases, but the base text's is the Torah's.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:13): ורגליו] omit EF; בשאול] במחשכי ABDEFG; תחתית] תחתיות ABDEFG; וחרוק] וחריקה C.
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'place him in a prison of darkness' — a third independent Hebrew handling of the destination.

verses.translation: The called{H7121} are many{H7227}, and the chosen{H977} few{H4592}.

one_way_hebrew: The saying already closed the vineyard-wage parable at 20:16 in this text; here as there it pairs Israel's calling-verb (קרא) with its election-verb (בחר, Deut 7:6-7).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:14): רבים] מרובים EF; מעטים] מועטים A.

verses.translation: Then{H227} the Perushim{H6567} went{H1980} and took counsel{H3289} to take{H3947} him in a word{H1697}.

one_way_hebrew: ויועצו (H3289) — 'they took counsel together': the psalmists' word for the plotting of the wicked against the righteous one (Ps 71:10, נועצו יחדו; Ps 83:6). Greek συμβούλιον ἔλαβον translates the scene into court-minutes.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ג (Perek 93) begins here; Howard notes: 'At this point the Brit. Lib. ms and ms C number this section פרק צ״ג, leaving out צ״ב, thus bringing their numbering system into line with the other mss' (see 22:1).
Howard's apparatus (22:15): בדבר] בדברו D.

verses.translation: And they sent{H7971} to him some of their disciples{H8527} with{H5973} Perushim{H6567} of Herodos, saying{H559}: Rabbi, we know{H3045} that you are faithful{H539}, and you teach{H3925} in faithfulness{H530} the way{H1870} of Elohim{H430}, and you are not anxious for any thing{H1697}, and you are no lifter{H5375} of faces{H6440}.

one_way_hebrew: ולא נושא פנים — 'no lifter of faces': the Torah's description of GOD himself — 'the great God... who lifts not faces (אשר לא ישא פנים) and takes no bribe' (Deut 10:17; cf. Lev 19:15 forbidding it to judges; b.Berachot 20a wrestles with the phrase). The flatterers describe Yeshua with the impartiality-formula Scripture reserves for the true Judge; Greek's οὐ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων is a calque of this idiom.
translation_notes: חושש — rabbinic Hebrew 'to be concerned, apprehensive' (chashash), a living-language verb with no biblical Strong's.
textual_notes: First occurrence in this chapter of אלקים — the ms uses the reverent ק-spelling to avoid writing the divine name outright.
The circulating transcription reads ורלמוד and נושה; Howard's text reads ותלמוד and נושא, corrected here.

Howard's apparatus (22:16): EF prefix ויועצו עם תלמידיהם; וישליחו] וישלחו CF; עם פרושים מהורודוס] omit D; פרושים] פריצים A ('violent men of Herod' — the Herodians; Howard's English follows A); האלקים] האלים A.

verses.translation: Say{H559}: what{H4100} does it seem{H7200} to you — is it right{H3559} to give{H5414} tribute{H4522} to Caesar, or not{H369}?

one_way_hebrew: מס (H4522) — Israel's own word for forced tribute, from Egypt's taskmasters (שרי מסים, Exod 1:11) to Solomon's levy (1 Kgs 5:27): a Hebrew ear hears bondage in the word. Greek κῆνσος is itself a Latin loanword (census) — each text names Rome's tax in its own borrowed coin.
translation_notes: לציזא״רי — Howard's edition prints the loanword pointed (לְצֵיזָא״רֶי); the points (and the spurious spaces they caused in the transcription) are stripped here, as elsewhere on this site.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:17): לציזאר] לשיזר A, לציזור B, לציזר CDEG, לציסר F; לך] omit G; אומר] + לנו G.

verses.translation: And they concealed{H2790} their cunning{H5231}, and he said{H559}: Why{H4100} would you put me to death{H4191}, hypocrites{H2611}?
words: would you put me to death

one_way_hebrew: נכל (H5231) — the deceit-noun from the verb of Joseph's brothers, 'they conspired (ויתנכלו) against him to slay him' (Gen 37:18) — and the base text's blunt 'why would you KILL me' says aloud what the plotting-verb implies: the tax question is a murder weapon.
translation_notes: The base ms reads ויחרישו את נכלותם... למה תמיתוני ('they kept their cunning silent... why would you put me to death'); mss ABDEFG read ויכר יש״ו את נכלותם ('Yeshua RECOGNIZED their cunning') and תסיתוני ('why do you incite/entice me' — סות, H5496, the enticement verb of Deut 13:7), matching Greek 'perceived their wickedness... why tempt ye me.' Howard's English follows the variants: '(Jesus recognized) their deceit and said: Why do (you entice me, hypocrites)?' The translation gives the base text; the letters ויחרישו are close to ויכר יש״ו, and the base may preserve a misdivision of exactly that.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads יוחרישו; Howard's text prints ויחרישו, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (22:18): ויחרישו] ויכר ישו ABDEFG; תמיתוני] תסיתוני ABDEFG; חנפנים] חנפים ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Show{H7200} me the coin of the tribute{H4522}. And they brought{H935} it to him.

translation_notes: מטבע — the rabbinic Hebrew word for a coin (matbea', from טבע 'to stamp'); the Mishnah's own term, unknown to biblical Greek or Hebrew.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:19): לו] + פשוט AG, + פשוט אחד D ('a pashut' — the medieval Hebrew name for a small common coin): the later scribes gloss the Roman coin with their own marketplace word, exactly as living-language copyists do.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Whose{H4310} is this{H2063} form{H6699} and the inscription{H7559}?

one_way_hebrew: הרשום (H7559) — 'that which is inscribed': Daniel's word (הרשום בכתב אמת, 'that which is inscribed in the writing of truth,' Dan 10:21). Greek ἐπιγραφή is a label; the Hebrew participle carries Daniel's scribal solemnity.

verses.translation: And he said{H559}: Caesar's. Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: Give back{H7725} to Caesar that which{H834} is Caesar's, and that which is Elohim's{H430}, to Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: השיבו (H7725) — 'give BACK, restore': the Torah's restitution verb (Lev 5:23, והשיב את הגזלה). Greek ἀπόδοτε ('render') is commercial; the Hebrew says the coin was never yours — return it. And what bears God's image must be given back to God.
textual_notes: The base text repeats לציזא״רי a fourth time ('give back to Caesar that which is Caesar's — to Caesar'); mss ABEFG omit the fourth occurrence. Howard's apparatus (22:21): לציזארי⁴] omit ABEFG; ויאמר] ויאמרו BG, אז אמרו EF; אליהם] להם AEF; ואשר לאלקים לאלקים] ולאלים אשר לאלים A; לאלקים²] omit B; the spelling of the loanword varies as at v. 17.

verses.translation: And they heard{H8085} and marveled{H8539}, and left{H5800} him and went away{H1980}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:22): וישמעו] omit EF.

verses.translation: On that{H1931} day{H3117} the Tsadoqim — the deniers of the resurrection of the dead{H4191} — called{H7121} to him, and asked him{H7592},

one_way_hebrew: תחיית המתים — 'the resurrection of the dead': the fixed rabbinic-credal term itself (m.Sanhedrin 10:1, 'he who says there is no techiyat ha-metim from the Torah'), with כופרים ('deniers'), the rabbinic word for those who deny a dogma. Greek must paraphrase ('who say there is no resurrection'); the Hebrew names the doctrine and the heresy in the Mishnah's own two words.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ד (Perek 94) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (22:23): ביום ההוא] בעת ההיא H; קראו] קרבו A ('drew near').

verses.translation: saying{H559}: Rabbi, tell{H559} us — Moshe{H4872} said: If brothers{H251} dwell{H3427} together{H3162}, and one{H259} of them dies{H4191} and has no son{H1121}, his brother{H251} shall take{H3947} his wife{H802} to raise up{H6965} seed{H2233} for his brother.

one_way_hebrew: כי ישבו אחים יחדיו ומת אחד מהם ובן אין לו — Deut 25:5 quoted letter-for-letter (כִּי־יֵשְׁבוּ אַחִים יַחְדָּו וּמֵת אַחַד מֵהֶם וּבֵן אֵין־לוֹ). Greek Matthew paraphrases the statute through Gen 38:8's Septuagint verb (ἐπιγαμβρεύσει); the Hebrew Matthew's Sadducees cite the Torah as Torah-readers do — verbatim.
textual_notes: ר׳ — the ms abbreviates רבי with a geresh, the standard rabbinic manner.
Howard's apparatus (22:24): אמור לנו] omit A; לקיים זרע אחיו] omit G.

verses.translation: And behold{H2009}, there were seven{H7651} brothers{H251} among{H996} us; and the first{H7223} took{H5375} a wife{H802} and died{H4191} without seed{H2233}, and his brother{H251} performed the levirate duty{H2992} for his wife{H802}.

one_way_hebrew: ויבם (H2992, yibbem) — the Torah's technical levirate verb (Gen 38:8, וְיַבֵּם אֹתָהּ; Deut 25:5,7). Hebrew has a single verb for the whole institution; Greek must spell it out (ἐπιγαμβρεύειν, 'marry the widow'). Only a text at home in Torah law talks like this.
translation_notes: אתים — so the printed text (a misprint for אחים, 'brothers,' as v. 24's אחים shows); retained as printed, with the transcriber's footnote concurring.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:25): והנה...בינינו] omit G; הראשון] + את G.

verses.translation: And likewise{H3651} the second{H8145} and the third{H7992}, until{H5704} the seventh{H7637}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:26): 'There is confusion in the text of G.'

verses.translation: And after{H310} them the woman{H802} died{H4191}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:27): ואחריהם] ואחרות B.

verses.translation: Since she already{H3528} belonged to all{H3605} of them, to which{H4310} of the seven{H7651} will the woman{H802} belong?

one_way_hebrew: שכבר (H3528) — 'since already': כבר is Ecclesiastes' private word (Eccl 1:10; 2:12,16; 3:15 — nowhere else in Scripture), and a staple of Mishnaic Hebrew. The question is phrased in the living Hebrew of the schools.
greek_deviations: The base text asks the question bare — 'to which of the seven will she belong?' — without Greek's 'in the resurrection' tag; ms A rewrites toward the Greek: ביום התחיה למי משבעתם תהיה לאשה שכבר היתה לכולם ('in the day of the resurrection, to which of the seven...').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:28): היה] היתה A, שהיתה BDEFG; אל מי] למי G; A rewrites the whole verse (see above).

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} and said{H559} to them: You err{H7686}, and do not understand{H995} the Books{H5612} and the power{H5797} of Elohim{H430}.

one_way_hebrew: הספרים — 'the BOOKS': Daniel's word for the Scriptures (בינתי בספרים, Dan 9:2). Greek γραφαί ('writings') is generic; a Hebrew reader hears the canon.

תשגו (H7686) — the going-astray of Ps 119:21 (השגים ממצותיך) and Lev 4:13; עוז (H5797) — 'strength,' the same word the text read in Ps 8:3 at 21:16: they do not understand the very עוז the psalm founded.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:29): ועוז] ועוד EF; האלקים] האלים A; תשגו] תנשו G.

verses.translation: In the day{H3117} of the rising{H8617}, men{H376} will not take{H3947} wives{H802} nor women{H802} husbands, but they will be like the messengers{H4397} of Elohim{H430} in heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: יום התקומה — 'the day of the STANDING-UP' (תקומה, from קום; the noun of Lev 26:37): resurrection named as the body's rising to stand. Beside v. 23's תחיית המתים ('the making-alive of the dead') the text commands both native Hebrew resurrection-words; Greek ἀνάστασις translates the first.
כמלאכי אלקים — 'like the MESSENGERS of Elohim' (מלאך, a sent one): as at 24:31,36, the Hebrew has no winged species, only sent ones.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:30): אלקים] אלים A; רק] אלא A; ולא הנשים אנשים] omit G.

verses.translation: Have you not read{H7121}, concerning the resurrection of the dead{H4191}, what YHWH{H3068} spoke{H559} to you, saying{H559}:

greek_deviations: 'What YHWH spoke TO YOU' — the ms writes the Name (ה״) where Greek has 'that which was spoken unto you by God' (ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ); and the word is spoken to the living hearers ('to YOU'), which is the whole argument.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:31): the repeated שאמר is omitted by ABEFH (G adds לכם); ה״] omit H; לכם] omit DG.

verses.translation: I am{H589} YHWH{H3068}, the Elohim{H430} of Avraham{H85}, the Elohim of Yitschaq{H3327}, and the Elohim of Yaaqov{H3290}. And if so, he is not the Elohim of the dead{H4191} but rather the Elohim of the living{H2416}.

one_way_hebrew: אני ה״ — the quotation opens with the Name itself: 'I am YHWH, the Elohim of Avraham...' — Exod 3:6 heard through Exod 3:15 ('YHWH, the God of your fathers... this is my name for ever'). Greek has only ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ θεός ('I am the God of...'). The argument stands on the living Name: the One whose name is 'He Is' cannot be the God of men who are not.
translation_notes: וא״כ = ואם כן ('and if so'); כ״א = כי אם ('but rather') — two scribal abbreviations in one sentence; the transcription misread the second as א״כ, but the scan reads כ״א, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (22:32): אני] omit G; אלקי (all five)] אלהי A (ms A writes the ה-spelling out); כ״א] כי H.

verses.translation: And the companies{H2267} heard{H8085} and marveled{H8539} at his wisdom{H2451}.

greek_deviations: 'They marveled at his WISDOM (חכמה)' — Greek Matthew has 'they were astonished at his TEACHING (διδαχῇ).' The Hebrew crowd hears chokhmah — the category of Solomon (1 Kgs 5:9-14).

verses.translation: And when the Perushim{H6567} saw{H7200} that the Tsadoqim had no answer{H4617}, they joined together{H2266}.

one_way_hebrew: אין מענה (H4617) — 'no answer': Job's phrase for silenced disputants (Job 32:3,5). The Hebrew narrator scores the debate as the book of Job scores Job's friends.
translation_notes: התחברו עבדיו — the base ms's עבדיו ('his servants') is a scribal corruption of יחדיו ('together'), as mss ABDG read (EF יחדו, C אחריו); Howard's English follows: 'they were gathered together.' The translation follows the sense.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״ה (Perek 95) begins here.

verses.translation: And one{H259} sage{H2450} asked{H7592} him, to test{H5254} him:

one_way_hebrew: לנסותו (H5254) — Massah's verb: 'wherefore do ye tempt (תנסון) YHWH?' (Exod 17:2,7); 'ye shall not tempt YHWH your God, as ye tempted him in Massah' (Deut 6:16). The tester tests the very One Deut 6 forbids testing — and the answer he receives (v. 37) is Deut 6:5, from the same chapter.
greek_deviations: חכם — 'a SAGE' (the rabbinic title) where Greek has νομικός ('a lawyer'): the Hebrew text speaks of the schools' own men.

verses.translation: Rabbi, say{H559}: which{H335} is the great{H1419} commandment{H4687} in the Torah{H8451}?

one_way_hebrew: מצוה גדולה שבתורה — the question is framed in the schools' own terms (the rabbinic ranking of מצות קלות וחמורות, 'light and weighty commandments'); the construction ש־בתורה is Mishnaic Hebrew syntax, not translation-Greek.

verses.translation: He said{H559} to him: You shall love{H157} YHWH{H3068} your Elohim{H430} with all{H3605} your heart{H3824} — and so on.

one_way_hebrew: The great commandment is given as the Shema's own words — ואהבת את ה״ אלקיך בכל לבבך (Deut 6:5), with the Name — and then the base ms breaks off with וכו ('etc.'): the scribe assumes every reader completes the verse by heart, as only a text written by Jews for Jews can. Where the mss do write it out (ABDEF), they write the TORAH's continuation — ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך, 'with all thy soul and with all thy MIGHT' — not Greek Matthew's, which reads 'with all thy heart, soul, and MIND (διανοίᾳ)' and lacks 'might' altogether. The Hebrew tradition completes the Shema from Deuteronomy; the Greek gospel had already drifted from it.
translation_notes: וכו — the abbreviation lacks its geresh in the printed edition (so the transcriber's footnote); rendered 'and so on.'
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads אלפיך; Howard's text reads אלקיך (the reverent ק-spelling of אלהיך), corrected here.

verses.translation: The second{H8145} is like{H1819} it: You shall love{H157} your neighbor{H7453} as yourself{H3644}.

one_way_hebrew: ואהבת לרעך כמוך — Lev 19:18 exactly, with the ל of the Hebrew original (love TO your neighbor) that Greek's ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου cannot show. The two commandments answer each other in the Torah's own openings: ואהבת... ואהבת.

verses.translation: And on these{H428} two{H8147} commandments{H4687} the whole{H3605} Torah{H8451} hangs{H8518}, and the Prophets{H5030}.

one_way_hebrew: תלויה (H8518) — 'hangs': the rabbis' own figure for dependence of many laws on few words (m.Chagigah 1:8, 'mountains hanging by a hair'; b.Berachot 63a, 'which is a small passage on which all the essentials of the Torah hang?'). Greek κρέμαται preserves the idiom because it translates it; in Hebrew it is the schools' native metaphor.
התורה... והנביאים — the Hebrew canon named by its own two divisions.

verses.translation: as it is written: The declaration{H5002} of YHWH{H3068} to my lord{H113}: Sit{H3427} at my right hand{H3225}, until{H5704} I set{H7896} your enemies{H341} a footstool{H1916} for your feet{H7272}?

one_way_hebrew: Ps 110:1 verbatim — נאם ה״ לאדוני — and only in Hebrew is the riddle sharp: the psalm distinguishes the NAME (YHWH, who speaks) from אדוני ('my lord,' who is enthroned). Greek reads εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου — 'the Lord said to my lord' — one word doing both jobs, the very distinction the argument turns on erased by translation. The Hebrew text of Matthew carries the psalm as David wrote it.
דכתיב — the Aramaic citation formula of the Talmudic academies ('as it is written'); no translator from Greek reaches for דכתיב.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 22 in the Shem Tov Hebrew: (1) The wedding feast is a חופה (chuppah, bridal canopy — Ps 19:6; Joel 2:16) seven times over, made by a king with no 'for his son' (v. 2, against the Greek); the refusers 'despise' it with Esau's verb (בזו, Gen 25:34, v. 5); the king burns their HOUSE, not their city (v. 7); and the speechless guest is cast 'into LOWEST SHEOL' — Deut 32:22's own phrase — where Greek has 'the outer darkness' (v. 13; mss ABDEFG shift to Ps 88:7's במחשכי תחתיות, toward the Greek). (2) The tribute scene: base text 'they concealed their cunning... why would you put me to death?' (v. 18; ABDEFG assimilate to the Greek 'perceived... why tempt me'); the coin is a rabbinic מטבע, later scribes glossing it 'a pashut' (v. 19); and the answer says 'GIVE BACK (השיבו) to Caesar' — the restitution verb (v. 21). (3) The Sadducees are defined by the Mishnah's own credal term — 'deniers of תחיית המתים' (v. 23; m.Sanh 10:1) — they quote Deut 25:5 letter-for-letter with the technical levirate verb ויבם (vv. 24-25), and the answer names resurrection twice in native words (תחיית המתים, תקומה) and clinches on the Name: 'I am YHWH (אני ה״), the Elohim of Avraham...' where Greek has only 'I am the God of' (v. 32). (4) The great commandment (v. 37) is the Shema with the Name — ואהבת את ה״ אלקיך בכל לבבך — broken off with וכו ('etc.'), a scribe's shorthand for a verse every reader knows; mss ABDEF complete it from the TORAH (ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך, 'might') where Greek Matthew reads 'mind' and lacks 'might.' The asker is a sage 'testing' him with Massah's verb (לנסותו, v. 35 — Deut 6:16 forbids exactly this, five verses before Deut 6:5); the Torah 'hangs' (תלויה) on the two love-commands — the rabbis' own metaphor (v. 40). (5) Ps 110:1 is quoted as written — נאם ה״ לאדוני — so the David's-son riddle actually works: the Name speaks to 'my lord'; Greek's κύριος/κυρίῳ blurs it (v. 44), and the quote is introduced by the Talmudic formula דכתיב. (6) Base-ms notes: the Brit. Lib. ms resumes at 22:1 and (with C) numbers the section פרק צ״א, betraying its lost leaf; פריצים 'violent men of Herod' in ms A at v. 16 (Howard's English follows); עבדיו for יחדיו at v. 34. Perek marks: vv. 1 (91/92), 15 (93), 23 (94), 34 (95).
